we have demonstrated that mutations in the gene for guanidino acetate methyltransferase (GAMT), an enzyme that catalyzes the final step in the biosynthesis of creatine, result in GAMT deficiency, a disease characterized by cerebral creatine deficiency, increased levels of guadinoacetate in urine, and mental retardation, by demonstrating that overexpression of the enzyme in GAMT-defective cells restored the activity of this enzyme.

we have shown that mutations in the gene for the enzyme GAMT are responsible for the disorder GAMT deficiency, by showing that overexpression of the enzyme restores enzyme activity in cells from patients with this disorder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional characterization of GAMT mutations and the identification of novel mutations.
the development of a functional test for the detection of GAMT variants.
the development and application of a novel method to study the molecular basis of human disease, i.e., the overexpression of the wild-type open reading frame of an affected gene in patient cells.
